fit_table.src: carbon rod in a resin socket: the 3.2 / 6.2 bores for 3 / 6 rods (CLAUDE.md), the resin fills the rest: it only has to go in (Overseer coupons v2, Spark 27 Oct: the largest of the coupon bores fit; OD + 0.3 was loose in PETG)

a D bore pressed on the N20's 3.0 / 2.5 D shaft: drawn 3.3 / 2.8 (+0.3 on the diameter and across the flat) pushes on by hand, a drop of CA (the probe coupon, Spark 14 Nov: D1 3.0 / 2.5 and D2 3.1 / 2.6 would not go on, D3 3.2 / 2.7 too hard to press home; printed holes come out ~0.1-0.2 small). min_gap: the drawn clearance per side the check accepts, 0.15 less the viewing mesh's 0.05 (D3's 0.1 failed by hand at 0.10 drawn, so a press mate is checked against the shaft's own D, not a round stand-in)
a bore turning free on an M3 axle or a 3 mm rod: 3.3 (coupon A1, the snuggest of 3.3 / 3.4 / 3.5, all free)
a bought body sliding into a printed pocket, sleeve or slot over its length (camera case, SG90 body): the axle's +0.3 plus 0.3 for the long contact and the case's own tolerance; check on the bench
a printed part sliding onto another printed part: both faces print GROW fat (0.2 of it gone) + 0.3 running
parts that pass each other and must never touch (an assembly path past a neighbour, a moving part)
a screw's shank through a printed clearance hole: M2 2.4, M3 3.4
a screw cutting its own thread in a printed pilot: M2 1.6, M3 2.6 (the SG90 tab pilots)

a screw's shank close-fit through a printed hole where it locates the part (the Overseer arms' M3 3.2 as the rod bore, overseer_arm_lib HOLE_D / SLOT_D; the carbon plates' Ø3.1 / 3.0 M; the hub deck's M2 2.2)
the resin injection port for one 14 G blunt tip (OD 2.11): Ø2.5 (Spark 8 Nov, CLAUDE.md; cage_node_lib PORT_R)
a hex nut's pocket across its flats: M3 5.5 -> 5.7 (overseer_arm_lib NUT_AF; not recorded in dimensions.md)

pairs.contact: the head's cable coil is drawn as a solid ring over the drum's O8 hub (a loose coil, nothing printed in it)
the blades leave the wound coil at its tangent (the feed drawn from the coil's surface)
the 40 / 12 gear mesh: the teeth are drawn at an arbitrary phase
the M3 x 5.7 heat-set inserts (drawn with the bolts) melted into the yokes' insert holes
the horn's hub on the SG90's spline, 0.25 off the case on the spline's shoulder (the spline itself not drawn)

mates.why: the cradle turns between the head frame's brackets
the pinion's D bore on the N20's 3.0 / 2.5 D shaft
the spool turns between the turret's side plates

paths.name: FC up onto its posts
paths.why: the FC on its grommets up from below onto its 4 posts (M3 into the inserts) with the receiver off (the battery mechanism bolts on after: its room is the boards' way in), the screws' heads from below

paths.name: XR2 up onto its land
paths.why: the XR2 taped up from below onto its land beside the FC with the receiver off (the battery mechanism bolts on after: its room is the boards' way in)

paths.name: DRV8833 up onto its land
paths.why: the DRV8833 taped up from below onto its land beside the FC with the receiver off (the battery mechanism bolts on after: its room is the boards' way in)

paths.name: Radxa up onto its posts
paths.why: the Radxa up from below onto its 4 posts (M2.5 into the inserts) with the receiver off (the battery mechanism bolts on after: its room is the boards' way in), the screws' heads from below; its tail third through the tail tray's window, before the UBEC (which hangs under it)

paths.name: UBEC up into its pod
paths.why: the UBEC taped up under its two end lands in the pod below the tail tray, after the Radxa (it closes the Radxa's way in)

paths.name: flow sensor up into its pod
paths.why: the MTF-02P taped up under its land in the nose pod, open below

paths.name: turret onto the frame
paths.why: the turret goes on as one unit with its spool, gears, N20 (into the deck's pocket), drum and roller (the DRV8833 is taped under the deck), down from above
